notes: Independent Athens tire-mold maker that has owned its Mill Street plant since 1969, idled production in 2011 and reopened in 2016 with a $400,000 JobsOhio revitalization grant and a pledge of 60 jobs over three years. Form 5500 shows 68 plan participants in 2023, so the company stayed under 100 employees through both grant years.

Single-purpose Columbus LLC formed in 2016 that took a $2 million JobsOhio revitalization grant and loan in fiscal 2018 with zero jobs retained; no JobsOhio release, Google News story or partner page names the project or developer. Bucket is a best guess for a real-estate project vehicle.

parent: Air South Commerce Center Phase II LLC (developer unidentified)
notes: Whitehall project LLC for a speculative commerce-center phase south of John Glenn airport, funded by a $2 million JobsOhio revitalization grant and loan in fiscal 2018-2019 with zero jobs retained. Searched the JobsOhio sitemap, One Columbus project pages, Columbus Underground and Google News for the developer and found nothing; bucket is a best guess for a project vehicle.

Nordson's FY2018 10-K reports 7,536 employees, incorporation in Ohio in 1954 and headquarters in Westlake; Xaloy was Nordson's screws-and-barrels unit at the 2018 grant. Nordson sold Xaloy to Altair Investments in 2020, which is why the 2023 Form 5500 sponsor is Xaloy LLC (340 participants) and the 2023 JobsOhio R&D release names Xaloy, LLC.

476 Bridge Street LLC is the affiliate of White Plains-based industrial real estate firm Reich Brothers that bought the 90-acre Columbus Castings (Buckeye Steel) site at bankruptcy auction for $29.7 million in August 2016 and held it until selling to Stonemont Financial in 2021, so the 2019-2020 grants funded cleanup of that South Side brownfield. Reich Brothers is a family-run acquirer with a small listed team and no public headcount, so the bucket is inferred from its website.

Privately owned Titebond adhesives maker founded in Columbus in 1935 and still headquartered at 2020 Bruck Street; Form 5500 shows 385 plan participants in 2019 and JobsOhio counted 372 retained Ohio jobs for the 2019 R&D grant. The company site now says 500+ employees (2025) and the 2023 plan count was 448, so it likely crossed 500 after the grant year.

Athens-based guitar-repair tools and parts maker founded in 1968, privately held with no JobsOhio metrics record for these grants. Form 5500 participants rose from 89 (2019) to 139 (2023), so the company was near the 100-employee line in the 2019 grant year and above it by 2021.

The bank is the subsidiary of Columbus-headquartered Huntington Bancshares, whose 2022 10-K reports 19,920 average full-time equivalent colleagues; JobsOhio counted 4,677 retained jobs for its revitalization and workforce grants. Huntington National Bank was founded in Columbus in 1866, though the holding company was organized under Maryland law in 1966.

Hamilton County village of about 2,800 residents that spent $9 million assembling land next to GE Aviation for its AeroHub advanced-manufacturing district, with Neyer Properties as master developer; the revitalization and OSIP grants funded that site work. Municipal staff count is not published in the sources found, so the bucket is a guess for a village government.

Big Heart Pet Brands is the pet-food subsidiary Smucker bought in 2015; Smucker's FY2021 10-K reports approximately 7,100 full-time employees worldwide and headquarters in Orrville, where the company was founded in 1897. JobsOhio's own release describes Smucker as an Ohio company for 125 years.

Operating LLC for DuPont's Circleville Kapton film plant, which employed 500 when JobsOhio backed a $200 million expansion adding 46 jobs; the 2020 10-K reports approximately 34,000 employees worldwide at Wilmington-based DuPont de Nemours. DowDuPont became DuPont de Nemours after spinning off Dow and Corteva in 2019, so it was the parent in the fiscal 2020 grant year.

parent: ExactCare Pharmacy LLC (Nautic Partners portfolio company)
notes: Valley View home-delivery pharmacy for chronically ill patients; Form 5500 shows 356 plan participants in 2019 and JobsOhio counted 185 retained jobs for the 2020 grants. Private-equity firm Nautic Partners invested in 2016 and later merged ExactCare with Tabula Rasa HealthCare in 2023 to form AnewHealth, which was after the grant year.

JobsOhio's release says Weastec employed 184 people at its Dublin and Hillsboro sites and operates as a subsidiary of Japanese electrical-components maker Toyodenso Co., Ltd., a Honda supplier. Weastec's own site says Toyodenso employs more than 10,000 associates globally; the Form 5500 count of 177 (2019) covers only the US unit.

Columbus-headquartered auto insurer that went public in 2020; the 2021 10-K reports 1,571 full-time employees at December 31, 2021, followed by a 20 percent workforce reduction in January 2022. JobsOhio's release describes Root as conceived in Ohio, and Caret Holdings is its Form 5500 sponsor (1,286 participants in 2023).

Columbus insurtech founded in 2016 and acquired by Madison, Wisconsin-based American Family Insurance in January 2021 (Business Wire, Columbus Dispatch), a year before the fiscal 2022 grant; AmFam's fast facts list about 13,500 employees for 2022. Bold Penguin itself had 78 retained Ohio jobs and 451 Form 5500 participants by 2023, so the 5000+ bucket reflects the parent, not the Columbus unit.

Privately held poultry processor headquartered in Troutman, North Carolina, whose four plants in Ohio and North Carolina employed more than 3,000 people per ProPublica's 2017 investigation; JobsOhio counted 346 retained jobs at the Winesburg plant for the $101.6 million expansion. Founder Thomas Shelton started the company in 1986 by buying the Winesburg, Ohio operation, so it began in Ohio though it is run from North Carolina.

Richfield-addressed LLC formed in 2020 that received a $1 million OSIP speculative-development grant in fiscal 2022-2023 with zero jobs retained. Searched the JobsOhio sitemap, Team NEO and Google News for a Richfield spec building tied to this name and found no release naming the developer; bucket is a best guess for a project vehicle.

Fountain Place is the former Macy's-anchored building on Fountain Square that nonprofit developer 3CDC bought in January 2019 (matching the LLC's 2018-2019 formation) and rebuilt as The Foundry, 150,000 square feet of office and retail; the OSIP grant supported that speculative redevelopment. 3CDC's 2023 Form 990 shows $12.4 million in non-officer salaries, consistent with a staff in the low hundreds, but the LLC's ownership by 3CDC is inferred from the project rather than stated in a filing.

Mentor project LLC formed in 2018 that received a $1 million OSIP speculative-development grant in fiscal 2022-2023 with zero jobs retained. The only Mentor release on JobsOhio's site is MUM Industries' own plant expansion, which does not name this LLC; searched Team NEO and Google News for a Mentor spec building and found no developer, so the bucket is a best guess.

Project subsidiary for the genetically engineered salmon farm AquaBounty began building in Pioneer, Ohio; the Maynard, Massachusetts parent's 2023 10-K reports 104 team members at December 31, 2023. The same 10-K says the Pioneer farm was about 30 percent complete with construction paused, so the grant's job commitments had not been met as of the filing.
